articles.title: Jaylen Brown Injury Update, Latest on 76ers Star's Status for NBA Cup Game vs. Pacers
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown will miss Friday's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers after leaving Wednesday's game with a hamstring injury, per ESPN's Kris Rhim.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown will miss Friday's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers after leaving Wednesday's game with a hamstring injury, per ESPN's Kris Rhim .

Meanwhile, Joel Embiid is questionable as he continues to deal with an illness.

The 76ers ruled Brown out for the remainder of Wednesday's contest against the Miami Heat with hamstring tightness after he played 17 minutes against the Eastern Conference foe. As the ESPN broadcast captured, he appeared to be in pain following a jump shot:

Brown struggled prior to the setback and was an ugly 2-of-8 from the field and 0-of-1 from deep for six points, one rebound and one assist.

It was a far cry from his recent play, as he dropped 31 points in back-to-back contests against the Pacers and Brooklyn Nets before scoring 20 points in a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. On the season, Brown is averaging 22.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.3 steals per game on the campaign.

With Embiid (when healthy), LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, the 76ers don't necessarily need Brown to dominate on a nightly basis like the Boston Celtics did last season when Jayson Tatum was sidelined.

Still, Philadelphia's ceiling is much higher when Brown is on the floor.

He is one of the best two-way players in the league with the ability to hit from the outside, drive the lane, take advantage of openings when defenders collapse on the other stars and guard the opponent's best players on the defensive side.

Fortunately for the 76ers, it is still early in the season in mid-November. There is no need to rush Brown back and risk further injury, and they will surely take a cautious approach following this setback.

For now, look for Maxey and James to carry more of the offense while Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope see more playing time.

articles.title: Líderes cristianos atacan a la "MAGA Barbie" de la WNBA por unas fotos: "Se sexualiza casi al nivel de..."
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham concedió un reportaje a Maxim en el que, a pesar de hablar sobre su fe en Cristo, ha molestado a líderes cristianos que han criticado sus fotos "al nivel de la pornografía"
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham concedió un reportaje a Maxim en el que, a pesar de hablar sobre su fe en Cristo, ha molestado a líderes cristianos que han criticado sus fotos "al nivel de la pornografía"
articles.body: La mediática Sophie Cunningham, que se ha convertido en agente libre tras ser la escudera de Caitlin Clark en las Indiana Fever de la WNBA, ha provocado el descontento de un grupo de líderes cristianos tras participar en una sesión de fotos para la revista 'Maxim' en la que posó en topless. La conocida como la "MAGA (Make America Great Again) Barbie" de la WNBA, por su apoyo público a Donald Trump y sus polémica declaraciones en contra de la participación de mujeres trans en categorías femeninas, habló abiertamente en la entrevista sobre lo que busca en un esposo y subrayó la importancia de encontrar a alguien que comparta su fe: "Tengo estándares muy altos para mi futuro esposo. Debe ser alguien centrado en Cristo, capaz de guiarme en mi caminar con Jesús". "Busco a alguien amable, seguro de sí mismo y firme. Busco a un hombre que pueda impulsarme en mi fe, que sea leal y que, además, ame cada pequeño aspecto de mi persona", subrayó. Sophie Cunningham confesó que le encantaría convertirse algún día en la comisionada de la WNBA, argumentando que el puesto debería ser ocupado por una exjugadora que entienda tanto las necesidades de las deportistas como el lado comercial de la liga. Otros planes tras su retirada de las pistas pasan por explorar el mundo de los comentarios deportivos (algo que ya probó en 2026), los pódcasts y ser entrenadora. Sophie Cunningham expresó su interés en convertirse en la "próxima chica Bond". El exnadador Riley Gaines, conocido activista conservador, ha propuesto a la "MAGA Barbie" como candidata a "chica Bond". La última "chica Bond", un personaje llamado Doctora Madeleine Swann, fue interpretada por la actriz Léa Seydoux en la película de 2021 'Sin tiempo para morir' (No Time To Die). A pesar de estas declaraciones líderes conservadores cristianos expresaron su desacuerdo con el hecho de que Sophie Cunningham posara en topless para 'Maxim'. "Ya no puedo compartir la opinión de quienes instan a las mujeres jóvenes a considerarla un modelo a seguir. No querría que mi propia hija o mis nietas hicieran algo así. El hecho de que ella se sexualice, casi al nivel de la pornografía, en las fotografías para la revista 'Maxim' hace que eso sea imposible. Me desconcierta por qué alguien haría algo así", declaró Robert George, jurista conservador católico y profesor en la Universidad de Princeton, en el 'Christian Post'. El evangelista Justin Peters denunció que "existe una falta de discernimiento entre los líderes del mundo evangélico, que elogiamos y damos plataforma automáticamente a cualquier celebridad que sea capaz de pronunciar el nombre de Jesús, sin tomarnos el tiempo de ver si su profesión de fe da algún fruto. Siempre, siempre termina volviéndose en nuestra contra. Por más veces que veamos repetirse la misma historia, nunca aprendemos". Sophie Cunningham le explicó a Drew Hanlen, en su podcast 'No Hesitation', las reservas que tuvo en un primer momento para posar para 'Maxim'. "Bueno, fue muy curioso porque, en mi propio mundo —no sé—, simplemente no estaba familiarizada con 'Maxim'. Se pusieron en contacto conmigo y les pasé la propuesta a mis agentes. Al principio, su respuesta fue: '¡Ni hablar!'. Me preguntaron: '¿Qué estás haciendo?'. Y yo les dije: '¿A qué se refieren?'. Resulta que ellos no sabían que 'Maxim' había cambiado su enfoque. Pensaban en la antigua 'Maxim', que es —bueno, hay que decirlo— una revista para hombres. Yo les dije: '¡Dios mío, chicos! Jamás se me ocurriría hacer algo así'. Pero, una vez que supieron que habían cambiado su enfoque, realizamos la sesión de fotos en Indianápolis. Me lo pasé genial; fue una experiencia increíble. De hecho, esos pantalones de cuero que llevo puestos costaban, si no me equivoco, unos 27.000 dólares. ¡Y hicieron falta cuatro personas para ayudarme a ponérmelos!" recuerda. Sophie Cunningham celebró en su cuenta de Instagram su portada en 'Maxim' con una publicación en su cuenta de Instagram: "¿Jugar a disfrazarse a los 30 años y terminar siendo la protagonista de la portada de una revista?». ¡Vaya! ¡Esto no ha hecho más que empezar! ¡Gracias, Maxim por contar conmigo como chica de portada! Me he divertido". Sophie Cunningham le reveló a Theo Von algo alarmante: ha recibido amenazas y ha sido víctima de acoso. La escudera de Caitlin Clark en las Indiana Fever asegura que el FBI está vigilando a unas 20 personas en relación con su seguridad. Un hombre de 49 años fue detenido en junio y enfrenta cargos graves por acoso e intimidación, además de un cargo menor por hostigamiento.

Kansas State basketball will look to bounce back and hope to give fans something to be thankful for when it takes the floor on Thanksgiving night.

The Wildcats will play No. 15 Alabama on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8 p.m. CT in a Players Era 16 tournament consolation semifinal at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas .

K-State was blown out 101-61 against No. 20 Gonzaga in the first round on Nov. 24, while Alabama lost 68-63 to Baylor right before. The Crimson Tide's 63 points were the fewest they've scored since 2023 .

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Admits He Was 'Upset' by NBA Rookie Rankings and Praises Kings' Darius Acuff Jr.
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Yaxel Lendeborg took it a little personally when he read his position in NBA.com's newest Rookie Ladder.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Yaxel Lendeborg took it a little personally when he read his position in NBA.com's newest Rookie Ladder .

"I saw the rankings today. I was No. 4," he told The Athletic's Devon Henderson . "I was a little upset about that."

Lendeborg did have plenty of praise for Sacramento Kings guard Darius Acuff Jr., who's sitting atop the Rookie Ladder.

"(Acuff) definitely got overlooked," Lendeborg said of the No. 7 overall pick. "Mine makes a lot more sense than his because I'm a little older, but he's the same age as all those guys and putting up the same kind of numbers. I don't know how you could pass up on him."

While the Kings are last in the Western Conference, it's not taking too much shine away from Acuff, who's averaging 24.4 points and playing nearly 37 minutes a night.

"I don't know how he's doing it so well," Lendeborg said. "For him, he's probably been dealing with that his whole life. Honestly, me, I've never really had that. I've always played off of somebody. It's different.

"I can only imagine how long it took him to adapt. It's crazy to see."

Like Acuff, Lendeborg is exceeding expectations out of the gate, but his performance is beginning to suffer a bit with Stephen Curry out of the lineup. He has shot 33.7 percent from the floor and averaged 13.7 points since Curry went down.

Acuff and Lendeborg crossed paths Wednesday night in NBA Cup play. Acuff nearly had a double-double, finishing with 22 points and nine assists. Lendeborg dropped a solid 15 points and eight rebounds.

Lendeborg at least claimed some bragging rights in the form of a 129-110 victory.

articles.title: No. 18 USC basketball drops its first game of the season in upset loss to unranked Utah State
articles.summary: The Trojans are now 7-1 and will take on Washington next Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Utah State Aggies are thankful to still be undefeated after their Thanksgiving matchup against No. 18 USC. The Aggies won 78-74 and moved to 7-0. The Trojans entered the game undefeated at 7-0 but suffered their first loss of the season.

This marked back-to-back close games for the Trojans. On Wednesday, USC narrowly beat unranked South Carolina 71-69, needing a late fourth-quarter comeback to secure the win.

That luck ran out Thursday night against Utah State in the Acrisure Series at Acrisure Arena in Palm Springs, California.

USC sophomore guard Alijah Arenas, son of former NBA guard Gilbert Arenas, led the Trojans in scoring yet again. He dropped 33 points and added 3 rebounds, 2 assists and a block.

The game was close on the stat sheet. USC shot 48% from the field and 32% from beyond the arc, compared to 45% and 29% for Utah State. The biggest difference between the teams was at the free-throw line. The Aggies made 18-of-22 attempts, while the Trojans took only 11 and made six.

Utah State was led by senior guard Mason Falslev, who finished with a team-high 27 points. Kingston Tosi provided a spark off the bench, adding 15 points and eight boards.

The Trojans will be back in action Wednesday against Washington (5-2, 0-0 Big Ten). Utah State will look to stay undefeated, taking on New Mexico (4-2, 0-0 Mountain West) on Sunday.

articles.title: No. 6 UCLA loses by 15 to unranked Saint Mary's for first loss of the season
articles.summary: Saint Mary's picked up a statement win that could easily factor into NCAA tournament seeding come March.
articles.body:
It is a bad day to be a ranked college basketball team based in Los Angeles.

Shortly after No. 18 USC was upset by unranked Utah State , the No. 6 UCLA Bruins lost to unranked Saint Mary's, 85-70.

The Bruins entered the matchup 6-0, but the Gaels had the right game plan, leading by 10 at halftime, and sustained that effort throughout the second half. UCLA kept it close at first, but Saint Mary's turned it on in the end.

Jaylen Petty led UCLA with 15 points, 7 boards and 1 assist. Xavier Booker added 14 points and eight boards.

The Bruins' problem was shooting from beyond the arc. UCLA shot 43% overall but just 29% from deep, hitting 5-of-16 attempts. By comparison, Saint Mary's shot 57% overall and 54% from 3-point range, knocking down 15-of-28 attempts.

Jeremy Dent-Smith led the Gaels with 21 points. One of the bigger sparks in the game came from Darius Bivins, who provided 16 points and five assists off the bench.

UCLA will look to shake off this loss as the Bruins return to action Tuesday, hosting Oregon for their first conference game of the season. Then, UCLA has a big non-conference matchup against No. 22 Gonzaga the following Saturday.

The win moved Saint Mary's to 7-1, as the Gaels have won five straight. They will next take on Hofstra on Tuesday. This victory over UCLA feels like one of those that we will remember at the end of the season when we break down Saint Mary's NCAA tournament résumé.

articles.title: Unforgiving rim denies Arkansas a miracle comeback against Michigan State on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: No. 11 Michigan State escaped with a 70-67 Thanksgiving win after Jordan Smith Jr.’s potential tying three rattled out in the final seconds.
articles.body: With 1:18 left in a game played on Thanksgiving, Arkansas trailed No. 11 Michigan State by 10 and the Spartans were at the free-throw line. If you’d offered John Calipari one shot to send the game to overtime, I’m guessing he’d have taken it before you finished the question. Well, he got his shot. Jordan Smith Jr. pulled up from 29 feet, and the ball found just about every part of the rim at Little Caesars Arena before it finally bounced out. Michigan State escaped Detroit with a 70-67 win to move to 6-1, and Arkansas fell to 4-3. Arkansas took a 31-27 lead into halftime, pushed it to eight early in the second half and still led 47-40 with 13:31 left. If you’re a Michigan State fan who watched the Spartans lose at Tennessee nine days earlier, I can’t blame you for thinking, "Uh-oh." They’d made all of three baskets in the second half in Knoxville and shot 18% for the game. MICHIGAN STATE'S PUTRID SHOOTING PERFORMANCE IN LOSS TO TENNESSEE PRODUCES LAUGHABLE FINAL BOX SCORE Down seven in Detroit, Jeremy Fears Jr. hit a three. Then he found Jesse McCulloch for a hook shot and Coen Carr for the dunk that tied it. Michigan State scored 15 straight, and by the time Kur Teng buried his third three in less than two minutes, the Spartans led 64-51 with 4:55 left. That’s a 24-4 run. The same team that went 3-for-26 after halftime at Tennessee went 17-for-21 (81%) in the second half against Arkansas. Michigan State still led 68-58 when Fears stepped to the line with 1:18 left. He missed the front end of a one-and-one, but Arkansas still needed 10 points just to pull even. COLLEGE BASKETBALL GETS A NEW NO. 1 AS THREE TEAMS FALL OUT OF THE AP TOP FIVE IN A SINGLE WEEK So how did the Razorbacks make it interesting in the final seconds? For starters, Michigan State just couldn’t grab a defensive rebound. The Razorbacks missed two threes on the same possession before Billy Richmond III tipped the ball in with 1:03 to go. Then Smith picked off a Fears pass. On the ensuing possession, Arkansas rebounded a missed free throw AND a missed three before Smith found Richmond for the three that cut it to 68-64. Arkansas gets a very generous and-one Jeremy Fears Jr. made both free throws with 16 seconds left to put Michigan State back up six. Then came the call I’d still be asking about if I were Tom Izzo. Smith drove to the basket and spun past Fears for a layup. The officials called Fears for a foul, counted the basket and gave Smith a chance to cut it to three with 10 seconds left. Did Fears foul Smith? Absolutely. Smith still had his back to the basket and was about 13 feet from the hoop when the contact came. Smith finished his spin, took another full step and then laid the ball in. How much continuation are we giving this guy? Even the CBS crew thought the foul should have been ruled on the floor. Smith made the free throw with 10 seconds left, Fears missed the front end of a one-and-one with eight seconds left, and guess who came down with the rebound? Smith had six seconds and the length of the floor to find a three. From 29 feet, he came about as close as you can get. A Thanksgiving bad beat for Michigan State bettors If you laid 5.5 with Michigan State, how good did you feel with 1:18 left? Your team was up 10, and you had a career 81% free-throw shooter at the line. You could give up a couple of garbage-time buckets and still cash. Fears missed the front end, Arkansas grabbed four offensive rebounds in two possessions, and Michigan State threw the ball away in between. And after all that? You were still covering when Fears hit both free throws to make it 70-64 with 16 seconds left. It took that generous continuation call to put Arkansas back inside the number. Then your 81% free-throw shooter went back to the line with eight seconds left and missed the front end of another one-and-one. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD That left Michigan State bettors rooting for the same guy who’d just cost them the cover. If Smith’s three drops, you get five more minutes to win by six. If you had Arkansas +5.5, on the other hand, you had every reason to cheer when that ball finally bounced out. Which probably raised a fair question from across the Thanksgiving table: "Wait, didn’t you bet on Arkansas?"

articles.title: El Movistar Estudiantes juega con ADN NBA para levantar el vuelo
articles.standfirst: La estadounidense Kendall Cooper, prima de Tony Smith y de Malik Monk, espera un Magariños lleno ante el Ibaeta en un encuentro crucial
articles.summary: La estadounidense Kendall Cooper, prima de Tony Smith y de Malik Monk, espera un Magariños lleno ante el Ibaeta en un encuentro crucial
articles.body: El Movistar Estudiantes comenzó la temporada en Liga Femenina Endesa disparando las expectativas con dos victorias en las dos primeras jornadas. Sin embargo, desde entonces las chicas de Isaac Fernández no han conseguido volver al camino del triunfo. Las Women in Black han mejorado en juego y prestaciones y ahora lo quieren trasladar al marcador final con una victoria ante el Ibaeta. Para ello quieren un Movistar Academy Magariños lleno este sábado. Una grada que empuje a un equipo en el que está destacando Kendall Cooper y que quiere remontar el vuelo al ritmo que marca la jugadora estadounidense. Máxima anotadora y segunda mejor reboteadora del conjunto estudiantil, la pívot de Carson está exhibiendo cualidades para el baloncesto que le vienen casi desde la cuna. De hecho le vienen por la parte de su familia materna. Una rama de su familia con ADN NBA como el que lucen Tony Smith, exjugador de Lakers con los que llegó a disputar la final de la NBA, y Malik Monk, número 11 del draft y que sigue en activo en las filas de los Sacramento Kings. Dos jugones que son el espejo familiar de Cooper. "Son mis primos por parte de madre. Somos muchos en ese lado de la familia”, apunta Cooper. "Su consejo es que nunca cambie mi forma de jugar. Siempre me dicen que esté concentrada y que juegue a mi manera. En el baloncesto profesional siempre hay gente que intente cambiar tu estilo de juego para que encajes en sus moldes. Lo que me dicen es que no cambie". Su primo Tony no sólo tuvo experiencia en la NBA durante su carrera deportiva. Tras pasar por Lakers, Heat, Suns y Hornets, Smith recaló en el TAU Vitoria en 1997. Apenas estuvo ocho partidos en la escuadra baskonista (9,5 puntos y 3,1 asistencias en 28 minutos) pero se le quedó grabado el ritmo de juego en el baloncesto español. “Una de las pocas cosas que Tony me dijo cuando le dije que venía a jugar a España es que estuviera preparada para correr, que aquí se juega muy rápido. Y no mentía al respecto. Creo que le subestimé cuando lo decía”, asegura entre risas la exjugadora de los Blue Devils de Duke. Adaptada ya a la velocidad de juego Cooper no se deja nada en el depósito cada vez que salta a la cancha. Por eso es una de las preferidas de la grada de un Magariños que espera ver lleno este sábado. “Cada vez que estoy en la cancha, lo que ves es quien soy. Me gusta competir, así que me esfuerzo al máximo para darle el 100 % de mí al equipo. Y si siento que todavía me queda algo de energía, lo doy todo”. Ahora sólo queda que ese esfuerzo se traduzca en una nueva victoria que daría vuelo a las colegiales. Para ello no existe una receta mágica, aunque Cooper da las claves para dar un paso adelante: “No existe una receta fija para que los equipos mejoren, pero, en nuestro caso, creo que necesitamos anotar. Trabajamos bien en conjunto en otros aspectos del juego; simplemente necesitamos meter el balón en el aro”.

articles.title: España echa cuentas: su gloria puede ser el drama de Grecia
articles.standfirst: El salto casi definitivo hacía el Mundial puede consistir en una victoria este domingo por más de tres puntos ante un combinado heleno que llega muy apurado: podría quedarse fuera
articles.summary: El salto casi definitivo hacía el Mundial puede consistir en una victoria este domingo por más de tres puntos ante un combinado heleno que llega muy apurado: podría quedarse fuera
articles.body: Las cábalas son múltiples a falta de tres partidos de clasificación y con tantas selecciones implicadas, pero España sabe que ganando este domingo (18.00 h, TDP y Vamos) en el Fontes do Sar a Grecia, si además supera el basket-average del partido de Atenas (-3), el pase al Mundial de Qatar 2027 estaría prácticamente en el bolsillo. Con esa sensación volará en las próximas horas desde Podgorica a Santiago, donde se reunirá con los internacionales del Madrid, Pradilla y Abalde, y con el del Anadolu Efes, Santi Yusta. Los tres jugaron sus partidos de Euroliga el miércoles. A España le saldrían las matemáticas si además de ganar le sonríen otros resultados: Georgia supera a Portugal en Tiblisi y Montenegro gane a Ucrania en Riga. En esas coordenadas, la clasificación puede estar prácticamente asegurada. El 'visado' a Qatar podría estar en la frontera de las siete victorias, con eso debe bastar. Una más lo asegura matemáticamente. A España le quedan, además del partido en Santiago ante el apurado combinado heleno, viajar a Portugal (26 de febrero, en Matosinhos) y recibir a Montenegro (1 de marzo, en una sede aún por decidir). Es jornada electoral, pero el Fontes do Sar estará lleno (quedaban dos decenas de localidades) para el encuentro que no sólo puede casi garantizar la presencia de España en el décimo Mundial de su historia, todos desde 1973 en Filipinas. La selección de Mateo puede apuntillar a la griega, que se presenta en Galicia apesadumbrada tras su derrota ante Georgia del jueves (88-92) con un pésimo juego. Spanoulis, el seleccionador heleno, no daba crédito para explicar la dinámica derrotista que envuelve a su equipo y que le afecta sobre la cancha, como ocurrió ante los georgianos. “Creo que tenemos que ver el partido contra Georgia y contar cuántas bandejas fallamos. Más de 10 o 12. Así es el baloncesto. Tenemos que seguir adelante. Es una derrota dura, y punto. Todo lo que podía salir mal, salió mal. Cometimos una violación de ocho segundos. Permitimos un triple de un jugador alto que nunca antes había anotado uno...” Si España lo tiene en la mano y podría meterse este domingo con un poco de fortuna, Grecia necesita la proeza de ganar al menos dos de los tres partidos que le quedan. Son urgencias épicas para una selección acostumbrada a estar en las grandes competiciones. No falla en un Mundial desde Indianápolis 2002. La ausencia es devastadora: tampoco podrá competir en Los Ángeles 2028. España está avisada de su peligrosidad, ahora que vive a la desesperada. “Sabemos que el partido del domingo es muy importante. Nos jugamos mucho los dos equipos. Podemos dar un paso definitivo hacia el Mundial”, resumía Pierre Oriola.

articles.title: Oregon men's basketball offense stalls late in loss to Texas Tech
articles.summary: Oregon failed to make a field goal in the final five minutes as Texas Tech rallied to beat the Ducks 62-59 in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Oregon's offense went cold and was unable to hold a late lead as No. 5 Texas Tech rallied to win Nov. 26 during a Players Era 16 Tournament men's basketball game at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas.

The Ducks didn't make a field goal in the final five minutes as the Red Raiders overcame a five-point deficit to win 62-59, sending Oregon to its third straight loss.

Jasper Johnson tied his season high with 18 points to lead the Ducks (3-3), and Andrew Meadow scored 13.

See photos from Oregon men's basketball vs Oregon State at Moda Center

Oregon trailed by 13 in the second half but went on 19-2 run to take a 54-49 advantage with 7:24 to play.

A layup by Fred Payne with 5:19 left in the game put the Ducks ahead 56-51, but that was their last field goal of the game as they missed their final five attempts, including a 3-point miss by Johnson with three seconds to play that would've tied the score.

Oregon outshot Texas Tech 42%-38.9% but was outrebounded 34-32 and allowed the Red Raiders to get 14 offensive rebounds and score 17 second-chance points.

The Ducks did have a season-high seven blocks, with Taylor Bol Bowen and Pharaoh Compton getting three each.

Oregon trailed by double digits at halftime. The score was 25-24 Texas Tech with just under four minutes to play in the first half, but the Ducks were outscored 13-3 over the final 3:24 and trailed 38-27 at the break.

What's next for the Oregon men's basketball team

The Ducks have one more game in Las Vegas at 12:30 p.m. Friday when they get an early season look at Big Ten opponent Maryland. The Terrapins are 3-4 after a 75-71 loss to San Diego State Thursday.

Chris Hansen covers University of Oregon football, men's basketball, track and field, cross country and softball for The Register-Guard. You can reach him at chansen@registerguard.com.

articles.title: Nets’ Moritz Wagner to miss Raptors game with knee issue
articles.summary: The Nets frontcourt is going from thin to downright worrisome, with backup center Moritz Wagner out with a left knee issue.
articles.body:
TORONTO — The Nets frontcourt is going from thin to downright worrisome, with backup center Moritz Wagner out with a knee issue.

Wagner left Wednesday's win in Milwaukee in the first quarter and was ruled out with left knee soreness. Now the only pure center the Nets have besides Day'Ron Sharpe will miss Friday's game in Toronto with left knee injury management.

"I was about to sub him in, and I saw him limping, and I was like I got to save him from himself," coach Jordi Fernández said. "He was there to do whatever it took for his team and his teammates, and at the end I decided to not bring him back in.

"The good thing — the great thing — is he was cheering for everybody. He was cheering for Grant [Nelson] the whole time, and that means a lot for the group, and it speaks to the type of person he is."

It's the same knee in which Wagner suffered a torn left ACL on Dec. 21, 2024. That ended his season and sidelined him until January 2026.

Sharpe logged 31-plus minutes Wednesday and could be asked to shoulder another heavy load against the Raptors, who've lost seven of eight.

He had 11 points and a season-high 14 rebounds against the Bucks, his fifth double-double to match his total from all of last season. Sharpe also added five assists and four steals.

"My effort, my motor is always going to be me," said Sharpe. "This is part of my game. It's a part of who I am, the hard work I play with, the hard effort I play with."

Nelson had just one point against the Bucks, but six rebounds, including three on the offensive glass. He was a plus-6 in just 13:04.

"The offensive rebounds for us were huge, six rebounds. He was a plus on the court, a great 13 minutes. He definitely was a big part of this win," said Fernández.

"Grant obviously not necessarily was expecting to go there for as much as he did," added Egor Dëmin. "But with Moe being out of the game, he had to go out there and compete. I talked to him in halftime and he was extremely ready to go, and just do what's best for the team."

Noah Clowney broke out of his extended funk against Milwaukee.

The young forward had 17 points and finished plus-14, both season highs. He shot 7-for-13, grabbed five rebounds and scored nine points in the fourth quarter.

"It was great to see him be aggressive, seeing the matchup he has and being aggressive off the closeout and just letting the ball fly when he had opportunity," said Sharpe. "He helps us out a lot, especially with the defensive presence he brings, his versatility on the offensive end. We just need him to continue to be confident in who he is and bring it out every night."

articles.title: Louisville HC Pat Kelsey gushes about ‘special’ Cardinals team after dramatic St. John’s win
articles.summary: The Louisville Cardinals survived a wild finish against the St. John’s Red Storm on Thanksgiving night, and head coach Pat Kelsey couldn’t stop raving about...
articles.body:
The Louisville Cardinals survived a wild finish against the St. John's Red Storm on Thanksgiving night , and head coach Pat Kelsey couldn't stop raving about his squad afterward.

No. 25 Louisville knocked off No. 13 St. John's 93-90 in the semifinals of the Players Era 16 Tournament at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, with Adrian Wooley burying a fallaway corner 3-pointer at the buzzer to hand the Red Storm their first loss of the season .

After the game , Kelsey explained what makes this group so special.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"This team is special… They're a group of dudes that just care about each other and just go to work like pros every single day. We don't have parent problems, we don't have agent problems… This team is a joy to coach. And they're fun to be around. It's player-led, just two unbelievably dynamic personalities and young men and leaders that are up here right now," Kelsey said, via The Field of 68.

The Cardinals had to dig deep to pull this one out. Louisville raced out to a 57-39 halftime lead and went up by as many as 24 points, but St. John's stormed back in the second half. Ian Jackson eventually tied the game with two free throws with 13 seconds left, setting the stage for Wooley's heroics.

Seth Trimble was the driving force for Louisville , pouring in a game-high 33 points on 12-of-19 shooting off the bench. Wooley finished with 19 points on 4-of-8 shooting from deep, while Karter Knox added 15 points and Flory Bidunga chipped in 12 points and nine rebounds.

For St. John's, Jackson scored 18 points, and Keyshawn Hall posted a double-double with 17 points and 10 rebounds.

The victory improved Louisville to 5-1 on the season. Still, Kelsey made it clear there is no time to dwell on it.

"And that was a big win, right? It was a big win for a lot of reasons. But we're in tournament play, and we celebrate it in the locker room. We turn the page, and we gotta get ready for our next opponent. And we're gonna play three games in three days," Kelsey added.

Louisville will face Tennessee in the championship game on Friday.

articles.title: Nate Oats reveals 1 thing Alabama needs to fix after beating Kansas State
articles.summary: Alabama improved to 6-1 after beating Kansas State, 104-91, in the Players Era 16 Tournament at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Thursday. The No. 15 Crimson T...
articles.body:
Alabama improved to 6-1 after beating Kansas State, 104-91, in the Players Era 16 Tournament at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Thursday.

The No. 15 Crimson Tide improved to 6-1, bouncing back from the loss to Baylor on Tuesday.

Seven players scored in double digits for Alabama, led by Qayden Samuel's 14 points off the bench. He added six rebounds. Amari Allen had 12 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, and two steals, while Drew Fielder and Anderson Diaz also scored a dozen apiece.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Coach Nate Oats was happy with his players' response coming off a defeat, as reported by BamaOnLine's Blake Byler.

"Good to get a win. We needed that after the loss to Baylor. Defensively, we're making strides. I thought we did a decent job outside of a few things," said Oats.

He, however, also pointed out a room for improvement , as quoted by BamaCentral's Hunter De Siver.

"We handled the physicality a lot better today than Tuesday. But at the end of the day, we've got to guard without fouling," added Oats.

Alabama committed 28 fouls. Kansas State went 28-of-37 from the free-throw line.

The Wildcats committed two more fouls than the Crimson Tide, who went 37-of-45 from the charity stripe.

Kansas State cut Alabama's lead to 10 points with 5:41 remaining in the second half. Allen, however, sank four straight free throws to fend off the rally.

The Crimson Tide led by as much as 19 points. They shot 51% from the field. They survived despite having 21 turnovers, which the Wildcats converted to 20 points.

Alabama will face Miami for fifth place on Friday.

articles.title: Pistons’ Cade Cunningham ruled out for Bucks game with knee injury
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons will have to go another NBA Cup matchup without starting point guard Cade Cunningham. Detroit has ruled out Cunningham for Friday’s game...
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons will have to go another NBA Cup matchup without starting point guard Cade Cunningham . Detroit has ruled out Cunningham for Friday's game at Little Caesars Arena against the Milwaukee Bucks due to his ongoing knee injury . This will be the third game Cunningham is forced to miss because of the ailment.

Cunningham went through shootaround before Tuesday's game against the Orlando Magic. He was listed on the injury report as probable prior to tipoff. After warming up with the team, the Pistons decided to sit the All-Star point guard for rest and recovery. Detroit head coach J.B. Bickerstaff briefly spoke on Cunningham's status before the contest against Orlando.

"He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that. He's gonna go out and compete and give us what he's got, but he's fighting through a lot," Bickerstaff explained.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Detroit continues to battle through the regular season as injuries have plagued some of their most important players. All-Star center Jalen Duren has been out since October due to a hamstring injury. Shooting guard Duncan Robinson has been out for the last five games after suffering a quad injury.

The Pistons are 11-6 and have found roster adjustments to keep winning despite injuries. Bickerstaff has used seven different starting lineups and has given every player on the roster playing time to fill in. Relying on the next man up mentality has been a big calling card for the Pistons this season.

There is currently no timeline for Cunningham's return to the court. The Pistons normally are patient and do not rush back injured players.
